items.stem: What is an ecosystem?
items.answer: An ecosystem is a self-sustaining system where biotic organisms and the abiotic environment of various communities interact with each other and exchange materials.

items.stem: State one advantage of using disposable paper cups over disposable plastic cups.
items.answer: Disposable paper cups are biodegradable, whereas disposable plastic cups are non-biodegradable.

items.stem: What are the two reasons for greater amounts of waste material generation?
items.answer: (a) Improvement in our life style. (b) Following western culture.

items.stem: Why has there been a large hue and cry against the use of CFCs?
items.answer: It is so because CFCs, when they reach the upper layers of the atmosphere, cause ozone layer depletion and allow harmful UV rays to enter the earth's lower atmosphere.

items.stem: Why is a forest considered a natural ecosystem?
items.answer: Forests are considered a natural ecosystem because they are natural regions that have species of plants and animals which interact with each other and are interdependent on each other. These are self-sustaining ecosystems, free of human interference.
items.ocr: Stray 'b' after 'Ans' in the printed answer tag dropped; 'selfsustaining' repaired to 'self-sustaining'.

items.stem: Name any two non-biodegradable wastes.
items.answer: Plastic bottle and polythene.

items.stem: Which of the following belong to the first trophic level? Grasshopper, Rose plant, Neem plant, Cockroach, Vulture.
items.answer: Rose plant and Neem plant.

items.stem: Why is a lake considered to be a natural ecosystem?
items.answer: A lake is considered a natural ecosystem as it consists of both abiotic and biotic components, which interact with each other.

items.stem: How do the changes take place in the environment?
items.answer: Environmental changes occur both due to some natural events and due to human activities.

items.stem: Name two instruments or devices in which CFCs are used.
items.answer: (a) Refrigerators, (b) Fire extinguishers.

items.stem: In the following food chain, 100 J of energy is available to the lion. How much energy was available to the producer? Plants → Deer → Lion.
items.answer: By the 10% law, only one-tenth of the energy passes to the next trophic level. So the deer had 1000 J and the plants (producer) had 10,000 J.
items.ocr: Reaction/food-chain arrows were dropped by OCR in 'Plants Deer Lion' and have been restored. The printed answer reads 'Plant (producer) will have 1000 J, while deer will have 1000 J' — the same figure twice, which contradicts the 10% law it applies; producer restored to 10,000 J.

items.stem: What is the formula of ozone?
items.answer: O₃
items.ocr: Printed 'O3' rewritten with a Unicode subscript as O₃.

items.stem: Which of the following materials are biodegradable? Glass, Leather, Glucose, Silver foil.
items.answer: Glucose and leather.

items.stem: In a food chain of frog, grass, insect and snake, assign the trophic level to the frog.
items.answer: The food chain is Grass → Insect → Frog → Snake, so the frog occupies the third trophic level.
items.ocr: LaTeX artefact '$\underbrace \mathrm{Grass} \to \mathrm{insect} \to \mathrm{Frog} \to \mathrm{Snake} \longrightarrow (\mathrm{Trophic level})$' rewritten into Unicode arrows; the trophic-level number was not printed and is read off the restored chain.

items.stem: What is the nature of ozone?
items.answer: It is deadly poisonous and a highly reactive oxidant.

items.stem: Select the biodegradable wastes from the following: DDT, Crop's residue, Leather and Glass.
items.answer: Crop's residue and leather.

items.stem: Give one protective function of forests.
items.answer: They reduce atmospheric pollution.

items.stem: Give some examples of an ecosystem.
items.answer: Forest, pond, ocean, etc.

items.stem: Name the organisms that form the first trophic level.
items.answer: Producers such as plants, algae, etc.

items.stem: What will be the amount of energy available to the organisms of the 2nd trophic level of a food chain, if the energy available at the first trophic level is 10,000 joules?
Name two substances which could not be broken down by the action of enzymes or microorganisms.
items.answer: (a) DDT, (b) Plastics.

items.stem: How many atoms of oxygen are there in ozone?
items.answer: Three atoms.

items.stem: What are the steps of a food chain called?
items.answer: Trophic levels.

items.stem: Which organisms are called producers?
items.answer: Green plants and cyanobacteria.

items.stem: The first trophic level in a food chain is always a green plant. Why?
items.answer: Because only autotrophs can utilise the radiant energy of the sun and transform it into chemical form as food during photosynthesis.

items.stem: List two main components of our environment.
items.answer: Abiotic and biotic.

items.stem: List two man-made ecosystems.
items.answer: Aquarium and park.

items.stem: Which of the following are always at the second trophic level of food chains? Carnivores, Autotrophs, Herbivores.
items.answer: Herbivores.
items.ocr: The book prints an 'or' variant of the same question in which OCR dropped letters ('second trophic evel of ood chains', 'Autotrophes'); the duplicate variant was merged into the single repaired stem.

items.stem: What is the self-sustaining unit of the environment?
items.answer: Ecosystem.

items.stem: Write the full form of UNEP.
items.answer: United Nations Environment Programme.

items.stem: Name the group of chemical compounds which adversely affect the ozone layer. Or, name the type of compounds which are used as refrigerants and in fire extinguishers and deplete the ozone layer in the atmosphere.
items.answer: CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons).

items.stem: List two biotic components of a biosphere.
items.answer: Animals and plants.

items.stem: Which of the following belongs to the first trophic level? Cockroach, wheat plant, cow, lion.
items.answer: Wheat plant.

items.stem: Define an ecosystem.
items.answer: An ecosystem is a self-sustaining unit made up of all the interacting biotic (living) components and abiotic (non-living) components of an area, which exchange materials and energy with one another.
items.ocr: The printed answer key for this question duplicates Q54's lake answer ('A lake is considered as a natural ecosystem as its consists of both abiotic and biotic components.'), which does not define an ecosystem; the definition printed by the same book at Q47 was used instead.

items.stem: What is environment?
items.answer: Environment is the physical, chemical and biological conditions of the region in which an organism resides.

items.stem: We often use the word 'environment'. What does it mean?
items.answer: Environment is the physical, chemical and biological conditions of the region in which an organism resides.
items.ocr: Printed 'the world environment' corrected to 'the word environment'; 'resider' corrected to 'resides'.

items.stem: Which one of the following organisms comprising a food chain will possibly have the maximum concentration of harmful chemicals in its body? Peacock, Frog, Grass, Snake, Grasshopper.
items.answer: Peacock, because it is the top consumer and harmful chemicals accumulate along the food chain by biomagnification.
items.ocr: Question begins on page 11 and its answer runs on to page 12; the page-break furniture ('## Page 12') was stripped.

items.stem: Phytoplankton → Zooplankton → Fish → Fish-eating birds. In the above food chain, which of the organisms will have (a) maximum available energy? (b) maximum concentration of pesticides?
items.answer: (a) Phytoplankton. (b) Fish-eating birds.
items.ocr: LaTeX wreckage 'P $\mathrm{hytoplanktons ~ ~ Zooplanktons ~ ~ Fish ~ ~ Fish-}$ eating birds' repaired: the split first letter rejoined and the dropped food-chain arrows restored.

items.stem: Name the disease caused in human beings due to depletion of the ozone layer in the atmosphere.
items.answer: Skin cancer.

items.stem: Mention any two methods of garbage disposal.
items.answer: Recycle and reuse.

items.stem: Give the full form of CFC.
items.answer: CFC stands for Chlorofluorocarbon.

items.stem: In a food chain, which trophic level has the maximum number of organisms?
items.answer: The first trophic level.

items.stem: Name two abiotic factors.
items.answer: (i) Light, (ii) Soil.

items.stem: What is the series formed of organisms feeding on one another called?
items.answer: Food chain.

items.stem: Use of paper bags is more environment friendly than the use of polythene bags for packaging. Justify.
items.answer: Because paper bags are biodegradable while polythene bags are not.

items.stem: Which of the following in a food chain will have the maximum concentration of harmful chemicals in its body? Small fish, Zooplankton, Bird, Phytoplankton.
items.answer: Bird.

items.stem: Why are green plants called producers?
items.answer: Because green plants (autotrophs) prepare their food through photosynthesis by using solar energy.

items.stem: Name any two main environmental problems.
items.answer: (a) Depletion of the ozone layer. (b) Disposal of wastes.

items.stem: How is depletion of the ozone layer in the atmosphere responsible for causing skin cancer?
items.answer: Ultraviolet rays of the sun, which can pass through the ozone hole, are harmful for our DNA and cause unwanted mutation, resulting in skin cancer.
items.ocr: Stray 'b' after 'Ans' dropped; printed 'nutation' corrected to 'mutation'.

items.stem: Is there any exchange of matter and energy between living and non-living components of an ecosystem?
items.answer: Yes, matter and energy are exchanged between the living and non-living components of an ecosystem.

items.stem: Give an example of a food chain of four trophic levels that exists in a grassland.
items.answer: Grass → Rabbit → Fox → Tiger, with the trophic levels being (i) Grass, (ii) Rabbit, (iii) Fox and (iv) Tiger.
items.ocr: The answer was printed as a LaTeX array ('$$\begin{array}...Grass Rabbit Fox Tiger...(i)(ii)(iii)(iv)\end{array}$$') with the arrows dropped; rewritten in Unicode with the arrows restored.

items.stem: What is the function of ozone in the upper atmosphere?
items.answer: Ozone shields the surface of the earth from ultraviolet rays coming from the sun.
items.ocr: The printed question number was lost (it was absorbed into the preceding LaTeX array block of Q97); number 98 inferred from position between Q97 and Q99.

items.stem: Name some of the waste materials.
items.answer: Vegetable and fruit peels, milk packets, polythene, paper, medicine strips, etc.

items.stem: Which two of the following belong to the same trophic level? Cockroach, spider, hawk, lizard.
items.answer: Lizard and spider.

items.stem: The depletion of the ozone layer is a cause of concern. Why?
items.answer: The ozone layer is very important for the existence of life on earth because it prevents harmful ultraviolet radiations coming from the sun from reaching the earth.

items.stem: Name two activities which form waste materials.
items.answer: (a) Preparation of food. (b) Industrial activities.

items.stem: Which one of the following belonging to a food chain is likely to have the maximum concentration of harmful non-biodegradable chemicals in its body? Phytoplankton, Fish, Kingfisher.
items.answer: Kingfisher, because it is the top consumer and harmful chemicals accumulate along the food chain by biomagnification.

items.stem: Write one negative effect on the environment of the affluent life style of a few persons of a society.
items.answer: An affluent life style results in the generation of excessive waste materials.

items.stem: Why are green plants called producers? Or, producers always occupy the first trophic level in any food chain. Why?
items.answer: Because green plants prepare food by photosynthesis, using solar energy in the presence of chlorophyll.

items.stem: Do the autotrophs (or producers) produce energy?
items.answer: No. Producers (or autotrophs) do not produce energy directly. They convert solar energy into chemical energy as food.

items.stem: "Man is only a consumer." Justify this statement.
items.answer: Man does not produce his own food. He feeds on stored food prepared by plants and on animals and their products, i.e. humans are heterotrophic consumers.
items.ocr: Missing closing quotation mark after 'consumer' restored.

items.stem: What are consumers?
items.answer: The organisms which consume food made by producers, directly or indirectly, are called consumers. Consumers do not make their own food. All animals, including human beings, are consumers. Common consumers are man, lion, cow, buffalo, etc. The consumers are also termed heterotrophs.

items.stem: What are omnivores? Give one example.
items.answer: Organisms which feed both on plants as well as on animals are called omnivores. Man eats both meat (animal) and plants (vegetables and cereals); therefore, man is an omnivore.
items.ocr: Printed 'man is an omnivores' corrected to 'an omnivore'.
